value.string: archimate-lite
Root for Lite tool-policy data in this package (allowed pairs, exchange notes). Not used in architecture diagrams.
AllowedRelationship rows; the single ExchangeSpec entity.
Declares one allowed (relationship type, source class, target class) triple for tool-side matrix checks. KC does not enforce it.
Assignment BusinessActor→BusinessRole; Serving TechnologyService→ApplicationComponent; DeployedOn ApplicationComponent→SystemSoftware.
Holds Open Exchange mapping notes for importers/exporters. Prefer a single instance with iriLocal=exchange-spec.
exchange-spec with catalogVersion, exchangeFormat, and DeployedOn/Risk/views rules.
Abstract root of all ArchiMate Lite concepts (elements, relationships, views). Do not instantiate directly.
Prefer a concrete subclass such as ApplicationComponent or Serving.
Abstract parent of structural/behavioral architecture elements. Instances are typed via instanceOf to a concrete subclass.
BusinessService, ApplicationComponent, Node, Risk — never ArchiMateElement itself.
Abstract parent of relationship entities. Each relationship is its own entity with relSource and relTarget.
Serving, Access, Flow, DeployedOn — create a relationship entity, not a free-form link.
Abstract parent of diagram/view constructs used to present the model.
DiagramView, ViewNode, ViewConnection.
business
An organizational entity capable of performing behavior — the owner, unit, or external party accountable for a system or service.
Business unit owning CRM; external payment provider; operations department; customer organization.
business
A responsibility that an actor may assume. Use for ownership and operating roles, not for technical accounts.
Business owner; system owner; on-call operator; compliance officer.
business
An externally visible unit of business behavior offered to customers or the organization.
Customer onboarding; invoice issuance; employee self-service; payment acceptance.
business
A sequence of business behaviors achieving a specific outcome. Use for key processes the system supports.
Order-to-cash; claim handling; identity provisioning request; month-end close.
business
Stable area of responsibility or work. Answers 'what is this unit accountable for?' — unlike BusinessProcess, which answers 'what happens when…'. Use as the primary business-layer decomposition.
Data Protection; Compliance Management; Customer Onboarding as a standing function (not a process run).
application
A modular, deployable application building block. At L0 model the whole system; at L2 split into frontend, backend, workers, etc.
CRM as a whole; web frontend; API backend; batch worker; shared microservice.
application
Application behavior exposed to the environment (users or other systems).
CreateCustomer service; SearchOrders; Authentication API capability; Reporting service.
application
A point of access where application services are made available to users or other applications.
REST /v1/customers; customer web UI; Kafka topic OrdersIn; SOAP gateway.
application
Automated behavior internal to an application component. Prefer when modeling internal capability, not a full workflow.
ValidateOrder; CalculateTax; HashPassword; IndexDocument.
application
An application-level workflow or batch sequence spanning one or more functions.
Nightly settlement batch; document OCR pipeline; password-reset flow.
application
An application-level state change of interest for integration or operations.
OrderCreated; PaymentFailed; UserLockedOut; CertificateExpiring.
application
A temporary or logical aggregation of application components cooperating as one unit.
Checkout collaboration (cart + payment + inventory); login collaboration (UI + IdP adapter).
application
A passive structure of data meaningful to the architecture (not every table or cache entry).
Customer master; order transactions; audit log; configuration store; search index.
technology
A technology capability used by applications — databases, identity, DNS, storage, messaging, load balancing.
PostgreSQL database service; Keycloak/IdP; corporate DNS; object storage; Kafka cluster service.
technology
An access point to a technology service that is architecturally significant (stable endpoints, VIPs).
DB listener host:5432; ingress VIP; Kubernetes API endpoint; DNS resolver address.
technology
A computational resource on which artifacts and system software are deployed (logical or virtual).
Application VM; Kubernetes worker node; bastion host; managed DB instance endpoint node.
technology
A physical ICT resource. Use when the physical appliance matters for DR, network, or ownership.
Physical server; firewall appliance; hardware load balancer; storage array controller.
technology
Software environment that hosts or runs application artifacts (OS, platform, middleware, DB engine).
RHEL; Kubernetes; PostgreSQL engine; JVM runtime; message broker runtime.
technology
A physical piece of data used or produced in deployment — images, packages, charts, config bundles.
Container image; Helm chart; Terraform module; signed config package; WAR/JAR release.
technology
A communication medium or logical network segment relevant to security/DR (VLAN, subnet, WAN, DMZ). Set networkKind from infrastructure/network depth (L3+); add cidr, vlanId, and networkRole at L4.
APP_NET VLAN 10.1.0.0/16 production; DC-WAN; DMZ; backup network.
technology

A named communication path between nodes or networks for impact analysis. Use Path when the route itself matters (WAN, replication link, zoned crossing) rather than Flow (what is transferred) or Association (membership or attachment).
DC1↔DC2 replication path; primary site to DR site WAN path; app-tier to DB-tier path spanning VLANs.
physical
A physical structure or environment such as a datacenter or technical building.
DC1 Prague; colo facility; head-office server room.
composite
A geographic or organizational place. Use when site matters for DR, latency, or regulation.
Prague; Brno DR site; EU-central region; branch office.
motivation
A statement of need that must be realized by the architecture (availability, RTO/RPO, compliance).
RTO ≤ 4h; RPO ≤ 15m; 99.9% availability; GDPR retention constraint.
motivation
Result of an analysis used to motivate decisions (criticality, maturity, health).
Business criticality = high; architecture fitness review; dependency risk score.
motivation
risk-and-security
A risk relevant to the architecture (Risk and Security overlay). Prefer for known SPOFs and threat outcomes.
Single WAN link between DCs; sole IdP without standby; unencrypted backup channel.
implementation
Difference between baseline and target architecture that a change initiative must close.
Missing HA for payment DB; no DR runbook for IdP; absent network segmentation.
implementation
A series of actions designed to achieve a goal within a defined timeframe.
CRM migration wave 1; network zoning project; HA database rollout.
Composition
Whole–part where the part has the same lifetime as the whole (strong ownership).
CRM system composed of Frontend+Backend+Worker; Node composed of Devices.
Aggregation
Whole–part grouping without shared lifetime (loose collection).
ApplicationCollaboration aggregating components; cluster aggregating nodes.
Assignment
Allocation of responsibility or deployment: actor→role, role→service, software→node, artifact→node.
BusinessActor→BusinessRole; SystemSoftware→Node; Artifact→Node.
Realization
More concrete element realizes a more abstract one (component realizes service/requirement).
ApplicationComponent→BusinessService; ApplicationComponent→ApplicationService; Device→TechnologyService.
Serving
Provider serves a consumer with behavior or capability. Preferred over Used-By for Lite models.
ApplicationService→BusinessProcess; TechnologyService→ApplicationComponent; Device→CommunicationNetwork.
Access
Behavioral element accesses a data object. Set accessMode to read, write, or readWrite.
Backend→CustomerData (readWrite); Worker→AuditLog (write); Reporting→Orders (read).
Flow

Transfer of information, value, or goods between elements — not a 'uses' or Serving relationship. Always set flowLabel (what flows). Use messageOrObject for the technical payload name; attach protocol/port/zone at L2–L4.
Backend→Payment Gateway (flowLabel=Customer orders, flowKind=data, protocol=HTTPS); WAN→APP_NET (Inter-DC replication).
Triggering
Temporal or causal triggering: source triggers target behavior.
ApplicationEvent→ApplicationProcess; Process A triggers Process B; schedule triggers batch.
Specialization
Generalization/specialization between elements of the same kind.
Generic ApplicationComponent specialized as PaymentGatewayComponent.
Association
Undirected structural link when no more specific relationship fits. Prefer specific types when possible.
Requirement↔ApplicationComponent; Node↔Facility; Facility↔Location; Node↔CommunicationNetwork.
Influence
Motivation influence: how an assessment or risk affects a requirement or service.
Assessment→Requirement; Risk→BusinessService.
Lite convenience for deployment. Exchange tools expand to Assignment (e.g. component→system software→node, artifact→node).
ApplicationComponent→SystemSoftware; Artifact→Node.
A named diagram/viewpoint over the model. Use viewpoint to distinguish catalog, dependencies, application, technology, network.
sys-crm catalog view; landscape dependency view; network zone view.
A visual node in a diagram, usually referencing an ArchiMate element via elementRef.
Box for ApplicationComponent; container group; free-text label node.
A visual edge in a diagram referencing a relationship entity and its source/target view nodes.
Line for Serving between two ViewNodes; Flow edge with bendpoints.
Marks the source element of a relationship entity. Required on every ArchiMateRelationship instance.
Serving where source is TechnologyService PostgreSQL; Access where source is Backend component.
Marks the target element of a relationship entity. Required on every ArchiMateRelationship instance.
Serving targeting ApplicationComponent CRM; Access targeting DataObject CustomerMaster.
Declares modeling granularity for an element (L0–L4 style). Prefer on every ArchiMateElement; shape aml-element warns if missing.
catalog for L0 system card; dr_minimum for L1 dependencies; application_detail; infrastructure_detail; network_detail.
Lifecycle status of the element in the estate (planned, live, retiring, etc.).
production; pilot; decommissioning; retired.
URI pointing to an authoritative external record (CMDB, ticket, docs).
https://cmdb.example/ci/123; https://wiki.example/systems/crm.
Which system is authoritative for this element's facts.
ServiceNow CMDB; Terraform state; DNS IPAM; manual architecture register.
Business or organizational owner accountable for the element.
Retail Operations; Head of Payments; Business unit XYZ.
Technical team or role responsible for running/changing the element.
Platform team; CRM guild; DBAs; Network ops.

Distinguishes an organizational unit, a named person, and an external party on BusinessActor. Required on every BusinessActor (shape aml-business-actor). department = org unit; person = named individual; external = party outside the organization.
department for Odbor Compliance; person for Petr Novák; external for EU Registry.
Who operates or owns the element: internal to the organization, an external provider, or a shared/multi-tenant service. EU registries and vendor SaaS are typically external.
internal for CRM Backend; external for EU Registry; shared for corporate IdP.
Business criticality classification used for DR and prioritization.
critical; high; medium; low.
Recovery Time Objective for the element or system.
Recovery Point Objective — acceptable data loss window.
15m; 1h; 24h; zero (sync replication).
Qualifies the kind of dependency expressed by a relationship (formalized enum/dependencyType).
runtime; data; identity; network; build-time; organizational.
Whether the dependency is mandatory or optional for degraded operation.
mandatory; optional.
What limited operation remains if the dependency fails.
read-only catalog; queue and retry; manual workaround; full outage.
Business consequence of failure of the dependency or element.
Cannot accept orders; delayed invoicing; login unavailable.

Qualifies the business meaning of an Association. Prefer a specific relationship type when one exists (e.g. Composition for org hierarchy). reportsTo is a reporting line between persons, not Composition. other requires relationshipNote.
reportsTo Petr Novák → Jiri Kreuzman; memberOf Node → CommunicationNetwork; spans Path → WAN.
Optional free-text note on a relationship. Required when associationKind is other.
Temporary dual-reporting during reorganization; exception approved by architecture board.
Communication protocol on interfaces, flows, or related concepts.
HTTPS; TCP; gRPC; Kafka; SMTP.
TCP/UDP port that is architecturally significant.
Whether an interaction is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous.
true for REST request/response; false for queue/event publish.
Authentication mechanism expected at an interface or flow.
OIDC; mTLS; API key; Kerberos; none (internal only).
Timeout policy relevant to resilience analysis.
Retry/backoff expectations for a dependency.
3 retries exponential backoff; no retry; at-least-once with DLQ.
Technical name of the message, event, or payload exchanged. On Flow this is the payload identifier; the business description belongs in flowLabel.
OrderCreated; CustomerDTO; PaymentRequest.
Business description of what is transferred by a Flow — 'what flows'. Required on every Flow (shape aml-flow). Do not confuse with messageOrObject, which is the technical payload or event name.
Customer orders; Inter-DC replication; Invoice PDF; Identity assertions.
Kind of Flow: data payload, event/message, control signal, or physical transfer. Use data vs event to distinguish request/response payloads from published events.
data for API or DB query; event for Kafka OrderCreated; control for health check; physical for media or material.
How a behavioral element accesses a DataObject (Access relationships).
read; write; readWrite.
Business/technical classification of a DataObject.
master; transactional; audit; reference; cache.
System of record that masters this data object.
CRM; ERP; IdP; locally owned by this system.
Retention period or policy for the data.
7 years; 90 days; GDPR erasure on request.
Whether the data can be rebuilt from upstream sources after loss.
true for derived search index; false for irreplaceable audit originals.
Whether backups are required for this data object.
true for customer master; false for ephemeral cache.
Information security classification of the data.
public; internal; confidential; restricted/PII.
Runtime environment name for deployed elements.
prod; staging; test; dr.
Cluster or platform grouping where the element runs.
k8s-prod-a; esx-cluster-01; managed-pg-cluster.
Logical namespace within a platform (e.g. Kubernetes).
crm-prod; shared-ingress; platform-system.
Runtime technology hosting the component.
JVM 21; Node 20; .NET 8; Python 3.12.
Configured replica/instance count for capacity and HA reasoning.
3; 2 (active-passive); 1.
High-availability pattern in use.
active-active; active-passive; none.
Primary operating site for the element.
DC1; eu-central-1a; Prague.
Disaster-recovery site for the element.
DC2; eu-central-1b; Brno.
Where deployment artifacts/config come from.
GitOps repo; CI pipeline; Helm chart registry; manual.
VLAN identifier for a CommunicationNetwork.
CIDR block of a CommunicationNetwork.
Security or network zone label. Prefer on CommunicationNetwork and Node so flows can be reasoned about by zone; sourceZone/targetZone on Flow should match these labels.
APP_NET; DB_NET; DMZ; MGMT.
Site affiliation for network or deployment concepts.
DC1; DC2; branch-42.
Routing domain or VRF name for a network.
corp-prod; pci; guest.

Type of CommunicationNetwork segment. Required at L3+ (shape aml-communication-network). Distinguish vlan (L2 segment), subnet (IP block), wan (site interconnect), dmz, overlay, management, and storage.
vlan for APP_NET; wan for DC-WAN; dmz for internet-facing segment; overlay for VXLAN.
Operational role of a CommunicationNetwork in the estate (production vs management vs backup vs dmz vs wan).
production for APP_NET; management for OOB/ILO; wan for DC interconnect; dmz for perimeter.
Fully qualified domain name of a significant technology interface.
api.crm.example.com; db.crm.internal; login.example.com.
Virtual IP of a load-balanced or floating endpoint.
Significant stable IP address (not every ephemeral node IP).
10.12.5.20; anycast DNS IP.
Reference to TLS certificate material for an interface.
vault:secret/certs/crm-api; ACM arn:…; internal PKI serial.
Source security/network zone on a Flow.
APP_NET; DMZ.
Target security/network zone on a Flow.
DB_NET; INTERNET.
Direction of a Flow relative to a trust boundary.
outbound; inbound; bidirectional.
Reference to the firewall/security policy governing a Flow.
FW-RULE-4421; Terraform aws_security_group.crm_db.
Viewpoint of a DiagramView — which concern the diagram serves.
catalog; dependencies; application; technology; network.
Links a ViewNode to the ArchiMateElement it represents.
ViewNode box → ApplicationComponent CRM; ViewNode → CommunicationNetwork APP_NET.
Kind of visual node in a diagram.
element; container; label.
X coordinate of a ViewNode bounding box.
Y coordinate of a ViewNode bounding box.
Width of a ViewNode bounding box.
Height of a ViewNode bounding box.
JSON-encoded visual style for a view concept (tool-specific).
{"fill":"#E8F0FE","stroke":"#1A73E8"}.
Parent ViewNode when nesting containers in a diagram.
Worker node parented under System container node.
Links a ViewConnection to the ArchiMateRelationship it visualizes. Required.
ViewConnection → Serving entity between API and IdP.
Source ViewNode of a ViewConnection. Required.
ViewNode for Backend as source of a Flow edge.
Target ViewNode of a ViewConnection. Required.
ViewNode for Database as target of a Flow edge.
JSON-encoded bend points for a ViewConnection path.
Annotation on an element class entity stating its ArchiMate layer. Written by catalog load/import, not on model instances.
business on BusinessActor; application on DataObject; technology on Node; motivation on Requirement.
Annotation on a class entity for ArchiMate overlays (e.g. risk-and-security).
risk-and-security on Risk.
Annotation on a relationship class with the Open Exchange xsi:type. Absent means non-standard (e.g. DeployedOn).
Serving; Access; Assignment — omitted on DeployedOn.
On an AllowedRelationship instance: the relationship class that is permitted.
Reference to Serving; Access; DeployedOn class IRI.
On an AllowedRelationship instance: permitted source element class.
Reference to ApplicationComponent; BusinessActor.
On an AllowedRelationship instance: permitted target element class.
Reference to BusinessService; SystemSoftware; DataObject.
Version string of the ArchiMate Lite catalog carried on ExchangeSpec.
Human-readable Open Exchange format note for tools.
ArchiMate Model Exchange File Format 3.1/3.2 XML.
Rule for mapping element classes to Exchange xsi:type.
class iriLocal (except Risk, View*, DeployedOn).
Rule for mapping relationship classes to Exchange xsi:type.
class iriLocal when exchangeType is set.
How DeployedOn should be expanded on Exchange export.
expand to Assignment.
How Risk should be represented in Exchange.
Risk and Security overlay type, or Assessment plus property overlay=Risk.
How view concepts map to Exchange view structures.
DiagramView / ViewNode / ViewConnection → views/diagrams/view.
How instance identifiers are chosen for Exchange.
iriLocal of instance, else entity_iri_alias kind imported, else public id.
